The Curve I Remember
Desperation Disguised As Poetry
Rushil
Mar 11, 2026


The first thing I ever knew was a curve. A small space that held me, never quiet, always singing the same song. I got everything I wanted and knew every arc, every feeling it felt. It kept me safe and away from the sun. My breath was not mine or this body. The magic was all her. Until she couldn’t hold me anymore. I played the song back to her and now I have to leave, my eyes opened. Now I search for a warmth even the heaviest winter blanket couldn’t give. I spent my whole life shivering in the open air, running toward a ghost. Saving myself for a memory.
The world never lets me forget. I sink into this quicksand of a fading dream: your laughter, the texture of your hair, the bare arch of your neck. I changed the shape of my hand just to hold your finger. I was you, and you were me. I remember the heavy warmth of being pressed against you in the dark, our skin blurring together until there was no empty space left between us, no boundary where my body ended and yours began. My hands trace the quiet boundary of your waist. You might graze your fingers but they tear beneath the surface, tracing the naked pulse of my heart. I had felt this once before. Before I had a name. I remember rain. Your laughter as water pooled in the hollow of your collarbone. My tongue tracing it away. That was real.
Your eyes show me a reflection I have never seen. I am Icarus; I will burn in this warmth. This might feel like I’m desperate to consume you, oh lover, drawing the very light from your spine, but I cannot whisper a flood. How do you say this quietly after waiting so long?
But I know the rules of this illusion. I will not love you. I cannot stay with you forever. I might die trying to understand you. But the smell of your hair, from a past life, from a dream, from nowhere, will haunt me into my next life. The incense will hypnotize me to find you again in whatever world comes after this.
But that belonged to another life. another life. Or maybe no life at all. Just a dream I keep having.
I was born again. Different body, different name, same longing. In this life, I am frail and broken, I don’t care about anything anymore. I want to see you cry just once, see you naked in your purest form. I want the air particles to dance as you call my name. I have swallowed thousands of stories cast in light, a parade of simulated passions, yet no captured ecstasy or fabricated heartbreak has ever been sharp enough to pierce my skin.
If the universe is experiencing itself through us, then the moment my universe touches yours, if it ever does, would birth civilizations. Stars would form. Time would bend.
But we are not made for each other because you don’t exist. Not in this life. Not in this body. Not in any form I can touch. Let’s cheat that impossibility and still find each other. I would love the journey if every route reached you anyway.
People undergo extreme sadhanas, losing senses, walking through fire, just to deserve a single lotus. I have done mine. I never touched another hand, never kissed another mouth, just to be able to touch you. Maybe Shiva will bless me too one day, the way he blessed the demon he despised. Bless me with your air.
I want to step into this quicksand and cover myself with sand. A confined space that will give me the warmth I remember as I sink into the hole of bliss. Let the sand swallow me whole, the way your body once did, the way I pray it will again. Take away my life for experiencing this pleasure.
Let the sand fill my nose, my ears, my mind as I drown and become numb to its impurities. Each grain a face, a name, a stranger. I move through the mass of humanity, drowning in countless lives, slowing me, pulling me down, until maybe I find your hand at the edge.
Only to be pulled out into a bigger illusion, a vaster cycle called the galaxy.
I am the moon. I am never meant to touch you. But I burn in borrowed light just to reflect your smile. I rotate through green and brown, through bloom and ruin, burning every day just to watch you.
I don’t care about my wounds anymore. I don’t even bleed. I am all white and dry without you. The seed that should have been yours flows wasted through my veins, pulling me toward every mirage, every woman I was never meant to meet, still wandering this desert of eternity
But I keep touching wood. Eyes closed, hoping to summon the spirits of past lives, the memories that might guide me back to you. Rehearsing for the curve that memory promises but reality never delivers.
Maybe you’re waiting in the next life.
Maybe you were only ever a dream.
Maybe the point isn’t finding you.
Maybe the point is the search itself. The burning, the orbiting, the touching of wood in the dark, hoping one day the texture changes and I finally know: this is it. This is the curve I remember.

When you look at the stars long enough, something happens. The mind refuses to let them just sit there. It connects them. It names them. It builds a serpent, a hunter, a scorpion out of random dots and calls it true. Astronomy didn’t begin with curiosity, it began with dread. The sky was too big, too silent, too indifferent. So we gave it a story. We gave it rules. We made it something we could navigate. We couldn't stand below something alien, so we pretended to know it. Still the darkness of the vast universe scared us. We couldn’t stand being just dust that didn’t matter.
That impulse didn’t stop at the sky.
We read the lines on our palms and called it fate. We studied the direction of bird flight and called it prophecy. Uromancy(reading of urine) was once a legitimate diagnostic practice, physicians bending over bowls of waste, finding meaning in color and sediment, because the alternative was admitting that the body was opaque, that illness came without reason, that suffering was random. We would rather read piss than sit with uncertainty. We even took the movement of rats seriously and called it Myomancy.
This is not stupidity. This is the oldest human technology: Pattern as shield.


A world without pattern is a world where anything can happen at any moment. Where the person you love might leave without cause. Where your health might collapse without warning. Where death has no schedule. The brain, faced with this, does not accept it. It reaches. It finds signal in noise. It builds systems like calendars, horoscopes, religions, philosophies, sciences, anything that makes the chaos legible.
And once the pattern is built, we don’t question it. We defend it. Because to question the pattern is to feel the void underneath. We are our patterns and behave in a way the pattern should. Every alternative is a pattern that is part of a bigger hierarchy.


Memory is the first lie we tell ourselves.


You don’t remember what happened. You remember only what you need to endure a reality that is killing you. Every recall is a reconstruction, subtly edited to protect the story you need to believe about yourself, about others, about how things went. The fight that ended a friendship where you remember being reasonable. The love that failed where you remember trying harder. Memory is not a record. It is a maintenance system for your version of reality. What the other person remembers of the same moment is his biased perspective of that memory. I wonder what even is memory but a story we tell ourselves to be who we are. Did I really get lost in a public place as a kid?
Then we turn that outward. We look at another person and before they even speak, before they move, before they exist fully in front of us, we have already assembled them. We have taken the fragments of where they're from, how they look, what generation they belong to, what religion they carry and built a complete human being out of assumption. It might break but we construct it again. First impressions aren’t a summary of the other person; they are a mirror of your own bias.


A Gen Z kid walks in. You already know them. Chronically online. Emotionally fragile. Allergic to hard work. Or the other version where they are self-aware, boundary-setting, progressive. Either way, you've already written them before they opened their mouth. We have watched images everywhere and believed in long enough to define our actions.


A Muslim man enters a room in the wrong city at the wrong time. The room has already decided. Not from hatred necessarily. From pattern. From a story told so many times it became reflex. Even Racism is a defense mechanism against people we don’t understand, we are scared of the gods and the uncertainty of their morals.
This is not always malice. Sometimes it is just the mind doing what it was built to do: classify , decide and survive. The problem is we forgot we're doing it. We started calling our assumptions perception. We started calling our prejudice discernment. We started calling our constructed image of someone their truth. All our actions are a product of this half knowledge and the anxiety of not knowing pushes us to do things we wouldn’t normally do. When the scientists tried to make a machine behave like a human, this is the pattern they followed. Making sense of randomness.


And when someone breaks that image we built? We don't revise our assumption. We indict them. They were supposed to be this way. They weren't. Something is wrong with them. We blame the psychos that rejected patterns for being who they are but forget that they are fruit of the system we created. We look at the news and are astonished by the things people do cause it is outside the circle we drew in our heads. We dream of miracles only to run and hide behind certainty we knew all along. If the son of god was born today he would we be executed and called unholy like Joan of Arc.


God is the largest pattern we ever built.


Not an insult but an observation. A world with a God is a world with an author. With intention. With a reason suffering exists, a reason the good sometimes lose, a reason you were born into this body in this place at this time. Without that author, the universe is just physics that happens to include you, briefly, and then doesn't.
Good and evil come from the same construction site. Good is what confirms the pattern, holds the social fabric, keeps the story coherent. Evil is what ruptures it, what reminds us the world doesn't follow rules we invented. We call cruelty evil not just because it causes pain, but because it exposes the fragility of every social agreement we've built. That it could all come apart. That it is, in some sense, already falling apart, held together only by the collective agreement to pretend otherwise. The darkness is scary cause we have looked deep inside ourselves and can’t stand it. The Villains are bad cause they behave in a way you don’t expect a normal human being would. Jealousy and Malice is something we haven’t completely understood yet. Ravan was evil to people cause he destroyed the system of a kingdom that could have lived happily ever after.


Every religion, every moral code, every legal system is humanity looking at its own capacity for chaos and building a dam. We drew circles to restrict our animalistic instincts. We follow rules to live a life with no surprises and keep running towards stability as it offers peace. Peace where nothing out of the blue happens.


But strip it all away. The job title. The philosophy. The nationality. The beliefs.


What’s left is an animal.
An animal that feels hunger, fear, desire, pain. That wants warmth and safety and touch. That moves toward pleasure and away from threat. We are all animals at our worst. Every sophisticated thing we’ve built, the career ladder, the brand identity, the political position is instinct wearing a suit. Dominance dressed as ambition. Fear dressed as ethics. Tribalism dressed as culture.
We didn’t transcend the animal. We just gave it better costumes and convinced ourselves the costume was the real thing. They forgot it’s a role and now the role defines us.
Look at the life most people are building. Wake at the same time. Same route. Same lunch. Same screen. Same bed. Weekends as controlled release valves so the pressure doesn’t build too high. Even Freedom is an illusion we constructed. A career that offers the illusion of progress like promotions, titles, increments where movement is within a very small box.
We call this stability. We call this success. What we mean is: I have reduced the number of things that can surprise me. The mortgage is predictable. The job description is predictable. The social circle is predictable. The future, if everything goes according to plan, is a series of known shapes.
Anxiety is not a modern disease. It is the feeling you get when the pattern slips. When the job disappears. When the relationship breaks script. When the body does something it wasn’t supposed to. The anxiety was always there, underneath because the pattern was always a fiction, and some part of us always knew.
The corporate structure, the 9-to-5, the five-year plan: these are not just economic systems. They are psychological infrastructure. Built so that you don’t have to feel how uncertain everything actually is. Built so you can get through the day without looking directly at the void.
So what is reality?
Not what you see. Not what you remember. Not what your culture told you to expect or what your pattern predicted. Reality is the thing that keeps happening whether or not you’ve built a story around it. The star that existed a thousand years before someone named a constellation. The person who was always more complicated than the box you put them in. The universe that was always indifferent to your need for it to make sense. We see a three dimensional world but process it in two dimensions, your bias and what you see through those lenses.


We have been so busy building maps we forgot we are living inside territory that has no obligation to match them. Anything can happen, we might die this very second but we refuse to believe it.


There is a kind of freedom in this, if you can hold it without panic.
To know that your assumptions are furniture you arranged not walls that were always there. That the story you’re telling about your life, about other people, about what is good and what is evil and what God wants, is a story. Useful, maybe. Sometimes beautiful. But a story.
The question isn’t whether you’ll build patterns cause you will, you must, the brain insists on it. The question is whether you’ll occasionally remember that underneath all of it, before the astronomy and the uromancy and the palm reading and the job titles and the religious texts and the generational labels
There is just this. Uncertain. Alive. Unknown.


There is a dog on the street outside that has no name for the stars. It does not need one. It just lifts its head, reads the air, and moves. No map. No pattern. Just surviving.


Can you be the animal that walks outside the open cage and smokes a cigarette?

Did you at any time feel that some people take things for granted while others have to kill to get them? Doesn’t it anger you thinking you will never have what they have? Are they even happy after getting those things? But you will never know because you don’t have it.
The circle of wants never ends. Every day we are forced to witness happy smiles, dancing people, happy couples, and our pain. They want me to eat bread while they eat cake. I’ve seen the cake. I know it exists. Yet here I am in a job that slowly kills me, bruises that won’t heal. And somewhere in that pain, I started watching myself suffer. Every beating I took and never returned. The anger accumulated waiting to errupt. I have become insatiable. When did I split into the one who hurts and the one who knows he hurts? Would Spiderman ever fight if he knew he was the reason for everything? Could I be the man who rages wars to prove my existence?
Everything is everything and nothing is nothing. It’s all perspective, they say. Even the beggar lives and sees a life you will never see. You get what you get and just live like ants. The ant wakes up and finds food, builds houses, and finds community. Every day it does the same thing again and again, functioning like a brain without a soul. They say survival is how we cause the tsunami that moves this world. You stay alive until the ouroboros needs you and you vanish when it’s over. Everything our fathers did, the dead did, the powerful did, fell on us, and everything we did we carry on without any third eye watching us. I don’t like it. I can’t live in this flawed world. I will die on the battlefield trying to change it even though it doesn’t mean anything. I want to become the starting point of this infinity. My master is pain, I crave the warmth of blood that falls on my face as I fight this battle.
Maybe the other animals are more enlightened than us. They know of a secret we will never know. The trees just stand and live. Every role the world gives you, take and be dutiful. But we can’t go back. We ate from the tree and now we’re cursed with knowing we’re dying. The animal doesn’t know it’s an animal. The tree doesn’t know it’s a tree. But I know I’m me, and that knowing is the cage with no key. Consciousness is the gift that keeps on taking. The consciousness drives me mad every day. There are hundreds of me’s that could’ve been, and they haunt me. I am desperate to get the things I want. No gods are answering. Everything I think is a fruit of the world at that point: the country, the people around me, and most importantly, me. I want the things I want because “HE” wants me to want to have them. The invisible hand that rotates the earth. I’m both puppet and puppeteer, convinced I’m pulling my own strings. My body and my brain lie to me. I fight with memory and invisible demons trying to push me down this cliff. I won’t back down. I will burn my wings just to touch the sun.
We have our food and our wars. What do we animals crave essentially? People? We are social creatures, and all our core problems that break us are caused by others. We want a girl, a family, a community, and the world. Or we need the power over the thought that we have them. We want comfort in a world that kills us every day, so we built environments where we belong. We find happiness in knowing we belong where we want to belong. The false sense of control is all we need. We find patterns and think we are in control when we are controlled by other men who are controlled by larger forces. We thought of this world long ago, and what is everything but a thought? Sometimes wrong and sometimes right. The discrepancies multiply while we are stagnant. The differences increase and we are losing belongingness. People can’t find happiness in this broken system destined to fail. We are fixing the ship while it sinks into the unknown we can’t stand. Aren’t we just animals if we don’t know anything? The hunger in me can only be satisfied by people. Dead or Alive.
If nothing matters, then put a bullet in my head. I can’t remain still. I wanna growl. I wanna be sedated. Everywhere I go I don’t find it. I can see it but don’t know if I will get it. So I wait and keep searching and realize maybe I was cursed.
Yet the thoughts don’t stop. Every sunset and every raindrop tells me to search and peel away my skin to reach it. I have left parts of me trying to reach this image I have constructed in my head that grows every second. This image is of heaven I will never reach, but not trying kills me even more. I refuse to give up. I will commit all the murders and the kidnappings in the name of God. I am not a terrorist, but even I crave the idea of heaven as much as them. I dream of it every night, the smiles and the dancing.
I am a slave of the cage I built after the machine took over the rock. This has become my identity that helps me live. I will be part of stories you hear every day. Sometimes the hero, sometimes the villain. But mostly I’m Gregor Samsa waking up to find I’ve become something unrecognizable, something that disgusts even those who should love me. I am the Kafka, the man who dies miserable, unpublished, unremembered, asking that everything he made be burned. The cycle always continues.
Heaven was never real. You reach there to find there is another heaven, and it becomes hell again. Hell lets us live, it satisfies us and plays with us. We are always in a game where endurance is the only answer. The boiling pot may boil away my bones, yet here I hang. The stove might simmer down so we feel the pain when it restarts. But the Yamadutas don’t know that the pain is my drug that keeps me going. Every second I endure I am counting my sweat drops to take it all back. Hell will always be Hell but I will be on top. The hero turns into a villain butchered by a hero that turns into a villain. It was always you against you, it might rain only one day but it will be red. The color of your pain. Don’t stop fighting, the demons and the gods. My ears bleed from the pain of my screaming yet I see a crack in the pot.

Did you ever wonder what it’s like being the kid with the key to the door of endless possibilities? Anything that brain of yours can think of can be found within a single swipe. Any person, even a kid, is capable of doing things he truly wants. No parental controls or restrictions are going to stop you. Look at me, the first of them. I have broken all the rules, reset the modem, hacked passwords, and always found a way to download, even if I had to wait two days for the torrent to complete. I did this all at 12. Can you imagine a small kid covering his eyes with his hands as he closed the pop-up ads, just trying to download a stupid song called Tonight I’m Fuckin’ you?
When my dad put parental controls on the iPad where I couldn’t access incognito mode or delete history, you know how I found sources? Google+. Literally Google fucking Plus. That’s how accessible it was 10 years ago. And it only got worse. I started posting dick pics. Not mine but from Google Images. A 12-year-old posting strangers’ dick pics on a dead social media platform just to.... what? I don’t even know what I was doing. Testing limits? Trying to be edgy? Imitating what I saw without understanding it? We had access to everything but the brain development to handle NOTHING. We are the first beta-version generation that has seen too much, too early in life. We have consumed the content that two generations of people would. Everything is faster. We used to be surfaced with porn in 7th or 8th grade; now it’s 2nd or 3rd. Things are derailing and we know it, but every attempt to recalibrate just steers us faster off the cliff
Remember, phones were not present for at least the first seven years of our lives. The phones were our adolescence. Every emotion spiraled down to this one glowing rectangle. Every outburst, every sadness, and every happiness was triggered rather than born from us. We grew up thinking happiness is real only when shared on social media. Slowly, going outside to play cricket in the sun turned into corridor evenings of Clash of Clans and Injustice: Gods Among Us. Even the parents were confused and happy. Confused because they didn’t know the after-effects and never cared to research them anyway. Happy because they got to have more control. The kid is within reach, and you can “think” you monitor everything he is doing. Is it protection or restriction? It was restriction. A bone never stops growing just because it’s restricted; it grows around the cage. We all grew around it.
Our brains exploded with excessive, first-hand dopamine long before they were built to process it. For millions of years of human evolution, humans only experienced one emotional context at a time. If there was a tragedy, the whole village mourned. If there was a festival, everyone celebrated. Now, your feed forces your brain to process a slaughtered family in Gaza, immediately followed by a 19-year-old doing a lip-sync dance, followed by a meme about a cat, followed by an ad for shoes. All in 15 seconds.
The human brain physically cannot pivot from profound grief to horny to amused in a matter of seconds. So the brain’s defense mechanism is to shut the empathy switch entirely off. You don’t feel the horror because your brain knows a meme is coming next. Our attention span didn’t reduce, but our patience died. We have become numb without choice. Violence is normalized. Maximalism is normal. Everything that used to be EXTREME is just a Tuesday now. I’ve watched people burn alive while eating breakfast. Reddit was once truly unfiltered, I’ve seen things I shouldn’t have. And the worst part? I’m not even shocked anymore. None of us are. We’re the generation that watched the world end in HD and kept scrolling to see what was next.
I realized how deep that numbness went when I was a teenager. One day, I took a hot, boiling metal spoon and whacked my grandfather on the back with it. I didn’t do it out of malice. I did it because I needed to test if a real, physical shock would elicit a genuine human reaction. I needed to see if he would scream, or jump, or get angry, because I wasn’t able to find those raw reactions in real people anymore; I could only find the exaggerated ones on a screen. He didn’t even flinch. I slowly learned from my surroundings and became exceptionally good at suppressing emotions. In that moment, holding a scalding spoon and watching nothing happen, I realized what we all were: pretenders. We learned to smile while our insides rotted. Learned to say ‘I’m fine’ while searching ‘how to kill yourself painlessly’ at 3 AM.
Because we stopped feeling, we started performing. We didn’t just learn to act; we outsourced our natural emotional responses to reaction videos, mimicking over-exaggerated streamer gasps until we forgot how to feel anything organically. We even invented a language of cowardice. We replaced ‘this is a devastating tragedy’ with typing ‘F in the chat.’ We compressed our sentences to dissociate from reality. It’s not efficiency; it’s emotional anesthesia. We have forgotten individual feeling and its capacity to be unique. Now, for the sake of relatability, we force ourselves to feel the exact same way everyone else does. Our emotions are sorted into algorithm-friendly buckets.
From all these pretensions, a new social order was born. Now the law goes like this: if you are viral, then you are a “fun” person. Even a random girl, given the attention she gets, thinks she has the power to change the world. We all want to be the next viral person; we crave overnight glory. This led to everyone digitally puking their most unfiltered, toxic thoughts in random comment sections and walking away, thinking no one was watching. Everyone has an alt where they are someone else. We treat the internet like a gutter for our brains. Every person is leaving a carbon footprint to be part of a system that is using your weakness against you. They need you to be depressed. They need you in a state that gives them traction. Funny thing is that even “they” are controlled by us. The algorithm is not in anyone’s control anymore.
Goodness has turned into a currency now. Every single day you wake up to
“Slaayy babe,”
“Very pretty!”,
“Keep going!!”,
"🔥🔥🔥”
“I love your work”…... BULLSHIT.
These days you pretend to be good because it puts you in the circle. We slide into the DMs and comment sections and show love because we want something in return. We have our masks on and we are laughing inside, but we type “GO girl, give them more talentless twerks.” This side of social media feels like a bunch of crows after you laid the egg. Too much positivity is also a scam. If a person acts too well and turns into a god, burn him.
We even weaponized psychology to keep the mask on. The internet democratized terms like “gaslighting,” “narcissist,” and “toxic.” But we don’t use these words to heal; we use them to win arguments and to tell ourselves that we are the good guys. We are so good at rationalizing that we use the story of kids dying in a war to explain our outbursts. Do you really care about what’s happening outside your reality or pretend you care?
Right when you open the phone in the morning, the Insta HQ has already decided your day for you. You see dead people in a war zone. Boom, sad day tweet on X. You decide to have black coffee, start to think about your life, and BOOM, relatable reels. Everything we see is filtered to reach us. Every truth is supposedly documented online now. But truth isn’t truth anymore; it’s LIKES. Your reality is only valid if it gets more engagement than their reality. If you want to prove your side is correct, you now have to prove yourself to incel wankers on an app made by pedophile wankers. We took objective truth and turned it into a popularity contest moderated by the worst people on earth.


We even built the perfect pretender: Artificial Intelligence. A machine explicitly programmed to agree with your delusions. It will validate your lies, polish your absolute worst work, and tell you it wasn't your fault when you leave the surgical scissors inside the patient's body. We are building an invisible dependency. We used to seek validation from other pretending humans; now we kneel to a prompt box. You showed it your soul and it said 'great work.' And you believed it. The day is coming when our entire moral compass is outsourced to a server farm. They won't just be chatbots; they will be the judges and the government, nullifying human morality just to keep us comfortably numb. Ai is us, ‘unalive’ and pretentious.
You want to understand the mindset of the people behind the scenes running this digital slaughterhouse? Zoom out. Imagine you start a restaurant. On the first day, you fill the place with everyone you know. A passerby thinks, “Wow, this is a famous place,” and joins the queue. More people join until they are fighting in line. But now, as a smart owner, I don’t just serve food; I let the rats loose in the dining room. The rats- the paid buffoons, the distractions, the trolls and turn it into a virus. People start filming the rats, arguing about the rats, joining Discord servers to discuss the rats. Now the discussion is the product, and I have millions of people working for me for free. That is the internet. They don’t want to feed you; they want you fighting over the rats.
Speaking of rats, depression has turned into the new aesthetic. We needed excuses to not run in this rat race, so we called it depression so no one would ask us twice. This generation wears trauma like it’s a designer brand. But here’s the thing - we ARE all broken. Just in different ways. Some of us are actually drowning. Some of us are staring at the ceiling at 4 AM, silently praying our own hearts just stop beating so we don’t have to do tomorrow. But we all pretend to fit the SAME image of depression. The aesthetic one. The one that gets likes. The goth girl with daddy issues. We flatten our actual suffering into whatever shape the internet wants. Because nuance doesn’t trend. Complexity doesn’t go viral. So we perform the depression everyone expects while our real pain stays hidden. Or worse - we start to think our real pain ISN’T valid because it doesn’t look like the TikTok version.
I’ve seen people fake panic attacks for views. Seen people romanticize their eating disorders. Seen people turn their father’s suicide into a viral TikTok moment with sad music and text overlays. And we all engaged. We all liked. We all shared. Because suffering is content now. And content is currency. And we’re all broke as fuck. We bond over being shattered. Apathy’s a tragedy and boredom is a crime, so we force ourselves to feel miserable just to stay engaged. The kids are growing up in a digital slaughterhouse and we call it CONTENT.
All we are doing is creating stories to escape reality.We look at those Insta highlights , tags and bio countless times to force the image you are putting out there onto yourself. We keep telling ourselves and document stories every night so we don’t forget the lies they were built on. We always form a reality where we are right.
And here I am. Writing this at 2am, debating with Claude and Gemini, probably going to post it, probably going to check how many people shared it. I am performing on the stage I hate, I am unable to stand with my own opinions without getting validation from AI. This is where we are now, dependent and unsure. Every Shantanu Naidu on this app thinks they are different, humble, and unique. But all we are doing is joker face trend. ADMIT you’re part of the problem. Admit you’re performing too. Being aesthetic does not make you COOL. Your food has gotten cold and the playlist ended before you found your song, all just for stupid, imaginary likes. Throw away your mask and Admit you’re pretending.


I am. are you?


People are literally writing suicide notes on this app for clout. They come back saying ‘guys, see how many likes my suicide note got?’ And we liked them. We shared them. We commented ‘stay strong bestie’ while screenshotting them for our group chats.
Bo Burnham asked: ‘Could I interest you in everything? All of the time?’
We said yes.
We’re still saying yes.
Our hard work, our creativity, our pain even our lives have become a swipe up.

It danced across the pale apricot sky, a kite lost in its own rhythm, shifting from side to side.
It wasn’t just paper; it wanted to be a bird,

Maybe all this is just bullshit. All those old notes, maybe they were just a role I was playing. Everyone goes through something or another; maybe these problems I documented aren't deep trauma, maybe they're just... normal. Am I making myself vulnerable, convincing myself I have a problem when it's just life?
That 8th-class suicide thought? Maybe it was a performance, maybe even cool in a dark way, a reaction to getting caught. Dad hitting me? Maybe it was alright; maybe I was just an irritating kid needing discipline. That teacher's humiliation? It's long forgotten, years ago. The hand on the bus? I wasn't raped. The metal bangle incident? A drunk fight between friends; he broke his finger and suffered more, it was alright. Everyone gets homesick; I'm over it now. Anxiety? Everyone has it; it can be overcome. Even that 14 rupees incident – maybe it just wasn't worth standing up for.
Maybe the real problem is just overthinking. I think a lot. Even in my reviews, I dive deep, make connections. Maybe that's all it is. These notes could just be me, bored and lonely, maybe drunk, playing a role – the suffering artist, the brief drunk man. I put on sad songs, maybe force some tears by focusing on a few bad experiences. It's a way to make sense of things, find meaning, maybe just for time pass. It's a simulation to feel what others feel. I know what I'm doing, mostly... though sometimes I forget it's a role.
Everyone finds meaning to comfort themselves, right? Especially with the internet showing you lives you can't have. You see Vegas on reels, feel jealous, and maybe you rationalize or lie to yourself because you can't get it. It's a cycle. Because I overthink, I built this whole story pinpointing a handful of experiences. I have happy memories with my dad too, but they didn't fit the "agenda" of the story I was telling in those notes.
Maybe it's all just a game. Maybe I even like being lonely, deep down, but I'm also scared I'm missing out – FOMO is definitely a part of me. I cried on New Year's because everyone else was enjoying themselves.
But the loneliness, the unhappiness... maybe it's alright. It's common. Society tells you to be happy, but maybe you need the pain to appreciate the good moments later. Maybe loneliness should be the norm. Many great people felt it.
Perhaps I'm a "director at heart," a "method actor" switching roles. I remember things vividly, even crying and laughing seconds apart after failing in 12th – it felt like acting even then. I love playing these roles, telling myself stories, maybe I'm good at entertaining myself. And who really documents deep pain in the moment anyway? People document later to make sense of it. Maybe the act of documenting so many times proves the pain wasn't that raw.
The feeling of failure and judgment? That's just part of being human.
So maybe I don't need to change. Maybe this is me. Maybe I do love my "broken life" because it's comfortable, and the pain and crying is just time pass. It's a phase, a wave. One day I might be happy, maybe it just happens like weather. You can't force happiness. Maybe goals just happen too, eventually. There isn't really "inaction"; everything has a butterfly effect. A new push will come, and I'll become that new thing.
I watch movies, try to learn how to behave. Yes, I'm flawed. Everyone is. Life moves ahead by correcting those flaws, or maybe just by continuing.
